source.title: ICSE 2025 Examination: Geography (H.C.G. Paper 2)
source.subject: geography
source.authorityName: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)
source.notes: No official marking scheme is published with this paper; questions carry no official answer. ICSE 2025 board examination paper; paper code 'T25 502' printed on every page; session 'Main examination' taken from the official bundle name (ICSE-MainExamination2025). 12 printed pages plus 1 outline map of India (PDF page 13). Part I (30 marks, compulsory): Question 1 (five 2-mark sub-questions) is topographical map work on the supplied Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S10, which is not in the PDF, so every Question 1 item is hasFigure true and confidence LOW; Question 2 (ten 1-mark items) is marking on the outline map of India, also hasFigure true and LOW; Question 3 is ten MCQs under a single printed [10], so 1 mark each is from the section instructions. Part II (50 marks): 'Attempt any five questions from this Part' over nine 10-mark questions (4-12); this is a pick-5-of-9 choice, not an OR pair, so choiceGroup is not used and the pack's marks total (120) exceeds maxMarks (80) by design. Marks are printed only per numbered sub-part ((i)-(v) / (i)-(iv)), not per lettered item, so each numbered sub-part is kept as one entry with its lettered items (a)/(b)/(c) in the text rather than guessing a split. No cognitive-level tags are printed. Question 3 (v)-(viii) on page 5 were checked in raw mode because layout mode separated the item numbers from their text.
source.usage: Official CISCE board examination paper from the CISCE Archive Library (cisce.org/archive-library); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

(b) Aman, a local craftsman, wants to sell his product to a large gathering to earn money instantly.
1. Which settlement should he go to?
2. Name the month in which he should visit the settlement named by you above.

questions.text:
The Ganga Plain is known for its fertile soil. It is often referred to as the food bowl of India. This region supports a variety of crops such as rice, wheat, pulses, jute and sugarcane.
(a) Name the soil that is found in large parts of Ganga plain.
(b) Give two properties of this soil which helps it to produce a variety of crops.

(a) What is meant by soil erosion?
(b) Name any two agents of soil erosion.

Give a geographical reason to explain each of the following:
(a) Soil conservation is the need of the hour.
(b) Red soil has a poor water retention capacity.
(c) Laterite soils are infertile.

With reference to black soil of India, answer the following questions.
(a) How is this soil formed?
(b) How is this soil able to retain moisture for a long period?
(c) Mention any two minerals present in this soil.

India has lost 2.33 million hectares of tree cover since the year 2000. This is equivalent to a six percent decrease in tree cover during this period.
Source: The Indian Express, Date: 12.04.2024
(a) Mention any two causes of the decrease in the forest cover of India.
(b) Name a conservation method that may be used to help in increasing the forest cover.
Mention the climatic condition suitable for the development of tropical evergreen forest.
State any three differences between tropical deciduous and tropical desert vegetation.

(a) Give any two reasons for the great diversity of natural vegetation in India.
(b) How do the forests help in maintenance of air quality?
Mention any one advantage and any one disadvantage of well irrigation.
Suggest any two measures to overcome scarcity of water in the metropolitan cities of India.

Give one reason to explain each of the following:
(a) Tank irrigation is NOT common in Northern India.
(b) Canal irrigation is important in Punjab.
(c) All farmers do not use tube well irrigation even if the geographical condition is favourable.
State any three objectives of rainwater harvesting.

With the rising price of fossil fuel every passing day, it is very important to develop non-conventional energy resource.
— Bulletin – Department of non-conventional sources of energy
(a) Name a non-conventional energy source that can be harnessed by taking advantage of India’s vast coastline.
(b) State one advantage of using geothermal energy.

(a) How is Biogas formed?
(b) Mention any one advantage of Biogas over other non-conventional energy resources.

Give a reason for each of the following.
(a) Iron ore is called a versatile mineral.
(b) Windmills set up on agricultural lands are beneficial to farmers.
(c) Coal is the most preferred source of energy in Indian industries.

(a) Identify the type of energy being generated in the picture given above.
(b) State why this type of energy is cheaper in the long run.
(c) Name a power project associated with the generation of this energy in the northern part of India.

(a) Mixed farming
(b) Zayad
(c) Transplantation

(a) Name the Iron and Steel industry located at Chhattisgarh.
(b) From where does the industry named by you above get its supply of the following?

(a) Which industry will he be writing about?
(b) Name any two by-products of the industry mentioned by you.
Why is a well-developed transport network important for India?
Mention any two advantages of road transport.

Name the following:
(a) The mode of transport that ensures comfortable journey, especially for elders and children.
(b) The highway connecting Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat.
(c) The cheapest means of transport for bulky goods.

(a) Airways are the most efficient mode of transport to connect Northeast India with the rest of the country.
(b) Railways are easily developed in the Northern Plains of India.
(c) Rivers of peninsular India are NOT ideal for inland water transport.

(a) Give a reason for a substantial rise of E-waste in India.
(b) What is dumping?

‘You cannot protect environment unless you empower people, you inform them and help them to understand that these resources are their own, that they must protect them.’
— Wangari Maathai (recipient of Nobel Prize 2004 for Sustainable Development)
As a responsible student how would you contribute to reduce and manage the waste generated in your surroundings. Explain by giving suitable examples.

With reference to the 3Rs, give a term that best describes each of the following:
(a) An empty soft drink can is used as a pen stand.
(b) Old scrap papers are used to manufacture handmade paper.
(c) No food is wasted in the household.

Give a reason for the following statements:
(a) Organic manure should replace chemical fertilisers.
(b) There should be a ban on the use of polythene and plastic products.
(c) Manual handling of waste must be avoided.
